Definition: from G303 and οἴγω (to open); to open up (literally or figuratively, in various applications):--open.
BiblicalUsage: To open: eyes, doors, mouths, heavens, and the book of life. Jesus says ask and it shall be opened unto you, the blind man's eyes are opened, the angel opens the prison doors, and the Lord opens a door in heaven before John. The word runs from the smallest opening to the greatest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe opening is God's work from first to last: He opens eyes that cannot see, doors that cannot be forced, and a heart that cannot open itself. I knock because He promised the door would open, and I hold that the open door in Revelation is the same promise, that no man can shut what Christ opens.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Man Born Blind; The Apostles Before the Council
